# Pins are the exact versions installed and exercised in this environment
# (Windows 11, Python 3.11.9, CPU-only measurement runs). Generated by
# grepping actual `import`/`from` statements under ceq/, scale/, tests/,
# run_calib.py, then reading versions off the installed packages -- not
# from PyPI's latest or from memory. Re-derive with:
#   python -c "import torch,transformers,numpy,scipy; print(torch.__version__, transformers.__version__, numpy.__version__, scipy.__version__)"
#   pip show <pkg>
#
# transformers is pinned tight (== not >=). ceq/hf/modeling_ceq.py sets six
# private PreTrainedModel attributes (_supports_sdpa, _supports_flash_attn,
# _supports_flex_attn, _can_compile_fullgraph, _no_split_modules,
# _tied_weights_keys) that are undocumented HF internals, not public API --
# they can change shape or be renamed in any transformers release, including
# a patch release. The colab notebook's `transformers>=5.0` has no ceiling
# and can install a transformers that silently drops one of these overrides.
transformers==5.3.0

# torch: installed build reads 2.14.0+cpu. The local version segment is only
# resolvable from download.pytorch.org, not plain PyPI, so the bare version is
# pinned instead -- installable as either the CPU or a matching CUDA wheel
# depending on the installer's index.
#
# This line read `torch==2.5.1` until this edit, while the interpreter ran
# 2.14.0+cpu, so the file's first sentence above was false for three of its
# pins (torch, numpy, huggingface_hub). Re-derived here with the command that
# sentence prescribes: `python -c "import torch,transformers,numpy,scipy;
# print(torch.__version__, transformers.__version__, numpy.__version__,
# scipy.__version__)"` reads `2.14.0+cpu 5.3.0 2.4.6 1.17.1`, and
# `python -m pip freeze` reads `huggingface_hub==1.30.0`.
#
# This file and `ceq/compat.py`'s REFERENCE answer DIFFERENT questions and are
# expected to disagree. REFERENCE names the stack the shipped figures were
# MEASURED on (torch 2.5.1+cu121, RTX 4060) and is provenance for those numbers,
# so it is not edited here. This file names what to install to run TODAY.
# `compat.version_record()["matches_reference"]` reads False on this box; by
# ceq/compat.py:211-214 that is a flag, not a failure, and it means no figure
# measured under REFERENCE is reproducible here until one of the two moves.
torch==2.14.0

# torchvision / torchaudio are NOT dependencies of this repository and are
# deliberately absent from the pins: `grep -rn "torchvision\|AutoImageProcessor\|
# AutoProcessor\|image_processing\|feature_extraction" --include=*.py .` returns
# zero matches across ceq/, scale/, scripts/ and tests/.
#
# They are nevertheless INSTALLED on this box as torchvision 0.20.1+cu121 and
# torchaudio 2.5.1+cu121 -- stranded leftovers of the torch 2.5.1+cu121 install
# that the 2.14.0 upgrade did not replace. torchvision 0.20.1's C++ extension is
# built against torch 2.5.1, so `import torchvision` raises
# `RuntimeError: operator torchvision::nms does not exist`, and that breaks 8
# test files at collection (re-measured 2026-09-20, WIN-16QAL06O9GB, python
# 3.11.9, torch 2.14.0+cpu, pytest 9.0.3; was documented as 10 here, but two of
# the original ten are gone from the tree and were never re-counted):
#   tests/chase/test_resume_checkpoint.py
#   tests/chase/test_scale_hazards.py
#   tests/gate0/test_g02_resume.py
#   tests/gate0/test_g03_persist.py
#   tests/gate0/test_g12_train_operator.py
#   tests/gate0/test_g13_beta_learnable.py
#   tests/gate0/test_g15_noise_floor.py
#   tests/gate0/test_g16_lrt_pinned.py
# Re-derive this list with (confirmed 2026-09-20, WIN-16QAL06O9GB, python
# 3.11.9, pytest 9.0.3, to return exactly these 8):
#   python -m pytest tests/chase tests/gate0 -q --collect-only 2>&1 | grep ^ERROR
# A grep for the string "torchvision" (or AutoImageProcessor/AutoProcessor)
# across tests/ is NOT a re-derivation: it returns zero matches (rc=1), same
# as the zero above for ceq/, scale/ and scripts/, because all 8 files reach
# torchvision transitively through transformers and never name it themselves.
# transformers 5.3.0 reaches torchvision
# unconditionally through modeling_utils -> loss.loss_utils -> loss_d_fine ->
# loss_for_object_detection -> image_transforms -> image_utils:53
# (`from torchvision.transforms import InterpolationMode`), so
# `from transformers import PreTrainedModel` fails behind it. The gate
# `is_torchvision_available()` tests only `find_spec("torchvision")`, which
# succeeds for a package that is present but unimportable, so no env var averts
# it: TRANSFORMERS_NO_TORCHVISION does not exist in 5.3.0 (zero grep hits in the
# installed package) and USE_TORCH/USE_TF do not gate this path.
#
# The repair is `pip uninstall torchvision torchaudio` -- removing packages
# nothing here imports -- NOT a pin, because no torchvision that matches torch
# 2.14.0 is present and installing one is out of scope for a file edit. Until
# then the 8 files above are RED and named; pytest.ini carries the count and
# the three causes.
#
# A collect-only count of this strand UNDERSTATES the true error total: as of
# 2026-09-20, tests/curvature/test_chess_probe_protocol.py yields 8 SETUP
# errors (`python -m pytest tests/curvature/test_chess_probe_protocol.py -q
# --tb=no` reads "8 errors in 1.70s, 0 passed, 0 skipped"), not the 1
# collection error a naive reading of "collect-only" would assume, because
# pi_jepa_chess.py is unstaged in this checkout. Any record that adds a
# collect-only number to this file's 8 and calls the sum the total error count
# is wrong by 8.

numpy==2.4.6
scipy==1.17.1

# Used by tests/foreman/test_topology_washout.py as the ripser/persim
# reference oracle for persistent-homology diagrams.
ripser==0.6.14
persim==0.3.8

# ceq/hf/train.py: `from datasets import load_dataset` / `from
# huggingface_hub import HfApi`.
datasets==4.8.4
huggingface_hub==1.30.0

pytest==9.0.3

# triton: imported at module scope in ceq/mz_kernel.py and tests/chase/k22.py
# and tests/chase/conftest.py, but only exercised behind
# `requires_triton` (needs CUDA compute capability >= 8.0) -- so on a
# CPU-only machine the import still has to succeed, it just never runs a
# kernel. PyPI has no `triton` wheel for win32; on Windows it is shipped as
# the community fork `triton-windows`, which is what's installed here.
# On Linux/macOS a downloader needs `triton` instead -- version not pinned
# below because no such install was available here to read a real version
# off of; do not guess a number, verify it on that platform before pinning.
triton-windows==3.7.1.post27; sys_platform == "win32"
